requirements.quote: An endpoint uses the Stream ID and Offset fields in STREAM frames to place data in order.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint processes data encapsulated in STREAM frames.
requirements.required_behavior: Use both the Stream ID and Offset fields to place stream data in order.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame-processing tests can vary Stream IDs and offsets and verify that data is assigned to the correct stream position.

requirements.quote: Endpoints MUST be able to deliver stream data to an application as an ordered byte stream.
requirements.condition: When delivering received stream data to an application.
requirements.required_behavior: Be capable of delivering the stream data as an ordered byte stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can deliver frames in varied orders and verify that the application-facing byte stream is ordered by stream offset.

requirements.quote: Delivering an ordered byte stream requires that an endpoint buffer any data that is received out of order, up to the advertised flow control limit.
requirements.condition: When stream data is received out of order and remains within the advertised flow control limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Buffer the out-of-order data as needed to provide ordered-byte-stream delivery.
requirements.why_checkable: Runtime tests can send in-limit stream data out of order and verify that it is retained until preceding data arrives.

requirements.quote: However, implementations MAY choose to offer the ability to deliver data out of order to a receiving application.
requirements.condition: When an implementation elects to expose out-of-order stream delivery to a receiving application.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation is permitted to offer out-of-order delivery as an optional application-facing ability.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's receive API and runtime behavior can be inspected to determine whether this optional delivery mode is offered consistently with the stated permission.

requirements.quote: Data that has already been received can be discarded.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives stream data that it has already received at the same stream offset.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to discard the duplicate data.
requirements.why_checkable: A duplicate-delivery test can verify that an implementation may discard already-received bytes without adding them again to application data.

requirements.quote: The data at a given offset MUST NOT change if it is sent multiple times;
requirements.condition: When data at a given stream offset is sent more than once.
requirements.required_behavior: Every transmission at that offset must contain the same data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending different data at the same offset in multiple transmissions.
requirements.why_checkable: Captured STREAM frames or sender tests can compare retransmitted bytes associated with identical stream offsets.

requirements.quote: an endpoint MAY treat receipt of different data at the same offset within a stream as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives different data for the same offset within one stream.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to treat the inconsistency as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can send conflicting bytes at an identical stream offset and the resulting connection-error type can be observed.

requirements.quote: Streams are an ordered byte-stream abstraction with no other structure visible to QUIC.
requirements.condition: When QUIC processes or exposes stream contents.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat stream contents as an ordered sequence of bytes without additional message or frame-derived structure.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Exposing additional stream structure as part of the QUIC stream abstraction.
requirements.why_checkable: API and runtime tests can determine whether stream data is exposed solely by byte order rather than as application-visible STREAM-frame units.

requirements.quote: STREAM frame boundaries are not expected to be preserved when data is transmitted, retransmitted after packet loss, or delivered to the application at a receiver.
requirements.condition: When stream data is transmitted, retransmitted after packet loss, or delivered to the receiving application.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame segmentation and application delivery could be observed, but the phrase "not expected" does not establish a definite required or forbidden implementation behavior.

requirements.quote: An endpoint MUST NOT send data on any stream without ensuring that it is within the flow control limits set by its peer.
requirements.condition: Before an endpoint sends data on any stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the stream data to be sent is within the flow-control limits established by the peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending stream data without first ensuring that it is within the peer's flow-control limits.
requirements.why_checkable: Sender tests can set peer flow-control limits and inspect emitted STREAM frames to verify that all sent data remains within those limits.
